content.title: About
content.content: Meat loaf made with beef is a baked dish prepared from ground beef, eggs, breadcrumbs, onion, and seasonings. It has a dense yet tender texture and a rich meaty flavor, often served in sliceable portions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally the loaf is baked in a loaf pan, giving it a bread‑like shape.
In the United States it is commonly topped with a tomato‑based glaze or barbecue sauce.
The recipe dates back to the 19th century as a way to stretch meat with breadcrumbs.
Some regional variations add cheese, vegetables, or mushrooms for extra flavor.
Meat loaf slices store well, making it a popular choice for school lunches and picnics.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Ground beef provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef contains heme iron, which is readily absorbed and supports oxygen transport.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is important for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Provides zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: The combination of protein, fat, and carbohydrates offers lasting satiety.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Large amounts of beef can raise cholesterol levels, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Salt and additives
items.content: Some recipes use a lot of salt or pre‑made sauces, increasing sodium intake.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: If breadcrumbs made from wheat are used, the dish is not suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Food‑borne bacteria risk
items.content: Improper cooking may leave the meat undercooked; ensure the internal temperature reaches 71 °C (160 °F).

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the meat loaf hot or cold, sliced thinly. It can be eaten on its own, in sandwiches, with vegetable sides, mashed potatoes, or salads. It pairs well with tomato sauce, mustard, or a honey‑mustard glaze.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the cooked loaf to room temperature, then wrap tightly in plastic wrap or place in an airtight container. Refrigerate for up to 4 days. For longer storage, slice and freeze portions – they keep well for up to 3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 71 °C before serving.
